title: World-Ego Modeling for Embodied Video Generation in Long-Horizon Navigation-Manipulation Tasks
abstract: arXiv:2605.19957v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Embodied video world models typically capture both scene evolution and the robot's behavior, which we refer to as the \emph{world} and the \emph{ego}, respectively. The world and the ego exhibit different underlying dynamics: world prediction relies primarily on visual history and emphasizes scene stability, whereas ego prediction relies more strongly on the current instruction and emphasizes accurate instruction following. Modeling both components within a single generation stream can entangle these different dependencies, making it difficult to specialize the prediction of either component. Consequently, it becomes difficult to simultaneously maintain scene consistency and accurate instruction following, particularly in long-horizon navigation-manipulation tasks. translated_abstract: 具身视频世界模型通常需要同时捕捉场景演化与机器人自身的行为，我们分别将其称为“世界”与“自我”。世界与自我呈现出不同的底层动态特性：世界预测主要依赖视觉历史，强调场景的稳定性；而自我预测则更依赖当前指令，强调对指令的准确遵循。在单一生成流中同时对这两个部分建模会使这些不同的依赖关系相互纠缠，导致难以对任一组成部分的预测进行专门化处理。因此，模型难以同时保持场景一致性与准确的指令遵循能力，在长时程导航-操作任务中尤其如此。本文提出将具身视频分解为“世界”与“自我”两个部分，并对二者的生成过程进行解耦。具体而言，我们将世界定义为……
tldr: 该论文提出将具身视频分解为“世界”（场景演化）与“自我”（机器人行为）两部分并解耦其生成过程，从而在长时程导航-操作任务中同时保证场景一致性与准确的指令遵循。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes decomposing embodied videos into "world" (scene evolution) and "ego" (robot behavior) components with disentangled generation processes, enabling both scene consistency and accurate instruction following in long-horizon navigation-manipulation tasks.
